newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan foreign reserves rose $5.52 bln in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan foreign reserves rose $5.52 bln in 1996.

text.p: Venezuela's foreign reserves rose $5.52 billion dollars in 1996, the Central Bank said, mainly as a result of large capital inflows stemming from higher international oil prices.
Reserves closed the year at $15.247 billion, up from $9.723 billion at the end of 1995.
They stood at $15.379 billion on January 7, the bank said in its weekly bulletin of indicators released on Friday.

A senior government official predicted last month that Venezuelan foreign reserves, with profit-sharing contracts in the oil sector and continuing strong oil prices, would grow about $4 billion this year to finish 1997 at around $20 billion.
